title: Ask Condenser: Runtime Prism Briefing (June 2026)
body:
Executive summary:

This note synthesizes a concentrated set of field signals from five mid-enterprise customers and several high-frequency self-serve customers between May 18–June 10, 2026. The thread is focused: customer-visible runtime friction (cold starts, KV cache misses, opaque token billing), short-term mitigation ideas, and a compact set of low-effort probes we can ship in the next 2–6 weeks to reduce incidents and lower perceived cost.

Why this matters:
- These customers are experimenting with high-concurrency chat workloads and report intermittent latency spikes that correlate with cache churn and model fallbacks.
- Several tickets show customers patching client-side retry logic to avoid perceived failures; that creates fragile integrations.
- Ops/CS overhead is increasing: multiple handoffs to SRE/Eng for the same root causes.

Key themes (ranked by frequency in signals):
1) KV cache thrash during variable prompt lengths (Top theme) — customers see dramatic latency variance when request sequence-length distribution changes rapidly (batching/eviction misalignment).
2) Model fallback confusion — when fallback to smaller/quantized variants happens, customers report degraded semantics and worry about silent quality regressions.
3) Billing transparency gaps — token breakdowns by system vs. user vs. cached tokens not surfaced; customers dispute spikes.
4) Observability granularity — per-route traces and request tags (customer_id, route_id) sometimes missing in export; harder to correlate cold-start vs. overload.
5) UX/Docs friction — engineering teams aren’t confident where to tune batching/cache settings for mixed-interactive workloads.

Representative customer quotes (redacted):
- "We saw a 450 ms tail spike after our nightly batch — it felt like the model just woke up and ate tokens."
- "Fallbacked model produced hallucinations on a billing-critical flow; we couldn't tell when it happened."
- "Your token bill doubled overnight and we have no visibility into how much was from cached prefixes vs live tokens."

Prioritized asks (customer-phrasing -> proposed low-touch probe):
A. "Make cold starts visible and actionable" -> Probe: add a cold_start flag in streaming responses + a short event emitted to customer metrics indicating warm/cold path. (Scope: telemetry + response header change)
B. "Give us per-request token decomposition" -> Probe: optional per-request token-breakdown endpoint for admin keys (JSON) that includes cached_prefix_tokens, fresh_tokens, system_tokens. (Scope: API + doc)
C. "Prevent silent fallback on critical routes" -> Probe: rollout route-level fallback policy: disable automatic fallback for routes marked non-fallback by customer (API toggle). (Scope: config surface + routing policy)
D. "Help us choose KV cache window sizes" -> Probe: heuristic recommender in Console that suggests TTL and shard size based on recent sequence length histograms. (Scope: analytics + UI)
E. "Lower tail latency for mixed workloads" -> Probe: small default batch-splitting change: when a route has >90% chat interactive traffic, prioritize latency-first micro-batches. (Scope: runtime policy)

Quick mitigations (2–6 week horizon, low engineering cost):
- Add a "warm_path" boolean to trace events and include it in the JSON response metadata for streaming (low).
- Expose an admin-only token-breakdown endpoint for last-24h aggregated requests (medium-low).
- Console flag to mark routes as "high-integrity" which disables automatic quantized-fallback (low).
- CS playbook: notify customers to set route tag ‘interactive=true’ for known flows to get latency-first batching (procedural, very low).

Engineering impact & risk notes:
- Telemetry metadata additions: minimal runtime overhead but requires storage/ingest schema bump. Need a quick data retention decision (30 days by default for the new flags).
- Token-breakdown endpoint: exposes internal accounting surface. Risk: need to avoid leaking internal model IDs or cost numbers for other tenants — admin-key gating and rate limits required.
- Route-level fallback toggle: small config change but interacts with autoscaler/resiliency policies — de-risk by making it opt-in and exposing fallback metrics.

Rough effort estimates (T-shirt):
- warm_path event + response metadata: S (1 engineer, 1 sprint)
- aggregated token-breakdown endpoint (admin-only, 24h): M (1–2 engineers, 1–2 sprints)
- console route flag + doc + CS runbook: S (owner: product+cs, 2 sprints for polish)
- routing policy opt-in for fallback prevention: M (1–2 engineers, coordination w/ autoscaler, 2 sprints)
- heuristic recommender for KV TTL: L (analytics + UI + model, 3–4 sprints)

Success metrics (how we'll know probes worked):
- 30% reduction in filed latency-related tickets from participating customers within 6 weeks of probe rollout.
- CS qualitative score: reduce "I don't know what happened" comments in post-mortems by 50% (sample of 10 incidents).
- Decrease in disputed billing tickets due to lack of token visibility by 70% for customers enabling token-breakdown.

Open questions / unknowns (to triage):
- Does adding warm_path flags materially increase telemetry payload and cost? (SRE input needed)
- How to present token decomposition without revealing proprietary cost allocation? (Legal/finance check)
- Will route-level non-fallback settings create availability regressions during regional outages? (SRE/Infra test required)

Next steps (owner/ETA):
- Product: create a scoped PRD for the token-breakdown admin endpoint (Priya, due 2026-06-28).
- Eng: prototype warm_path response metadata and add opt-in logging (Elliot, spike by 2026-06-18).
- CS: identify 3 customers who will participate in early validation; prepare runbook (Samira, list by 2026-06-17).
- Compliance/Finance: short review of token-breakdown exposure (Marta, reply by 2026-06-20).

Notes to self / worklog snippets:
- TODO: add link to telem schema PR once opened.
- Note: customer "AtlasHealth" wants route-level SLA; consider mapping their needs to Dedicated capacity brief.
- Slack thread: #cs-runtime-asks has a long thread starting 2026-05-23 — paste highlights into PRD.

Appendix: short example response (developer-friendly) -- illustrative only:
{
  "id": "req_XXX",
  "warm_path": false,
  "token_breakdown": "admin-only-exposed-separately"
}

End of briefing.

If this resonates, I recommend we move the warm_path telemetry + admin token endpoint into a single scoped milestone for July to maximize CS signal capture before Q3 renewals.
